title: Additive maps and dot products
statement: Let $f$ be a map from the $n$-dimensional vector space over $ br/2 br$ to $ br/2 br$. Then $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$ for all vectors $x,y$ if and only if there is a vector $a$ such that $f(x)=\\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i x_i$ for every vector $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps $( br/2 br)^n$ to $ br/2 br$
